w: On 26 June 1907, a Bolshevik gang led by Stalin's ally Simon Ter-Petrosian -- 'Kamo' -- ambushed a State Bank stagecoach here with bombs and guns, killing forty, netting 241,000 rubles for the cause. Lenin and Stalin had both quietly backed the plot, then scrambled to deny it once the party condemned the bloodshed.
s: A Bolshevik bank heist backed by Lenin and Stalin
_facts: Site of the 1907 Tiflis bank robbery, an armed Bolshevik attack on a State Bank cash shipment on 26 June 1907
Led by Simon Ter-Petrosian, known as 'Kamo,' the raid killed forty people and netted 241,000 rubles
Organised by top Bolsheviks including Lenin and Stalin, who distanced themselves once the party condemned the killings

w: Founded in 1851, one of the oldest opera houses in Eastern Europe, and since 1896 housed behind a neo-Moorish facade hiding a European hall inside. Fire has damaged it more than once; the latest six-year restoration wrapped in 2016 at a cost of forty million dollars. Named since 1937 for composer Zacharia Paliashvili.
s: An Eastern Europe opera house wearing a Moorish mask
_facts: Founded in 1851, among the oldest opera houses in Eastern Europe
Housed since 1896 in a neo-Moorish building on Rustaveli Avenue, though laid out like a typical European opera house inside
A six-year restoration, costing around $40 million, concluded in January 2016
Named since 1937 for composer Zacharia Paliashvili

w: An artificial lake built in 1953, nearly nine kilometres long, that Tbilisi never quite treats like plumbing. What started as a reservoir for the city's water supply turned into its favourite weekend escape, ringed with beaches and picnic spots -- with more sports facilities and parkland still planned for its shores.
s: Tbilisi's 1953 reservoir, now its favourite beach
_facts: Artificial lake and reservoir near Tbilisi, 8.75 km long, opened in 1953
Became a popular recreation spot
Plans exist to develop it further into a recreational park with sports facilities

w: One museum umbrella covering most of the country's cultural memory: since forming in 2004, it has folded in the Simon Janashia Museum, the Museum of Soviet Occupation, and archaeological reserves at Dmanisi and Vani. One director, David Lordkipanidze, has run the network since day one.
s: One roof over most of Georgia's museums
_facts: Formed on 30 December 2004, unifying several of Georgia's leading museums
Directed since its founding by professor David Lordkipanidze
The network includes the Simon Janashia Museum, the Museum of Soviet Occupation, and archaeological reserves at Dmanisi and Vani

w: Georgia's largest and among its oldest theatres, opened in 1887 behind an ornately Rococo facade on the avenue that shares its name. It didn't take the name Rustaveli until 1921, borrowed from the medieval poet whose epic verse is Georgia's founding literary myth -- a fitting patron for the country's grandest stage.
s: Georgia's grandest stage, named for its national poet
_facts: The largest and one of the oldest theatres in Georgia, founded in 1887, housed in an ornate Rococo-style building on Rustaveli Avenue
Has carried the name of national poet Shota Rustaveli since 1921

w: Established in 2006 to document seven decades most Georgians lived through but rarely discussed out loud: Soviet rule from 1921 to 1991, and the repression that came with it. Now folded into the Georgian National Museum, it exists to remember the people who resisted occupation -- and the ones who didn't survive it.
s: Documenting seventy years of Soviet rule in Georgia
_facts: History museum documenting Soviet rule in Georgia from 1921 to 1991
Established on 26 May 2006, dedicated to victims of Soviet political repression and the national-liberation movement
Part of the Georgian National Museum

w: Chronicles from the 11th to 13th centuries knew this stretch of the Mtkvari's east bank as Isani, long before anyone called it Avlabari. Old Tbilisi's low-rise sprawl is now one of the city's hippest districts, gentrifying fast enough that the medieval name and the trendy cafes share the same streets.
s: Old Tbilisi's medieval quarter, now going hip
_facts: Neighbourhood of Old Tbilisi on the left bank of the Mtkvari River
11th-13th century chronicles refer to it as Isani
Now an upcoming, extensively gentrifying district

w: Built originally as the Imperial Russian gendarmerie's headquarters, this Avlabari building spent decades after independence as the president's official residence. As of 2026 it has changed hands again, now housing the Ministry of Foreign Affairs -- swapping occupants more often than most Georgian institutions.
s: A Tsarist police HQ, later Georgia's presidential seat
_facts: Formerly the Avlabari Presidential Residence, housing the administration of the President of Georgia
Located in a refurbished building of the former Imperial gendarmerie on the left bank of the Kura River
Since 2026 houses the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Georgia
